description: 2 tactical challenges for White against the Schliemann Gambit. Meet 3...f5 with calm development and punish Black's overextension.

drills.briefExplanation: 3.Bb5 f5 4.Nc3 fxe4 5.Nxe4 d5 6.Nxe5 — develop, centralize, and let Black's pawn weaknesses tell.
drills.description: White to play. Black is threatening the wild 3...f5 — pin the knight and be ready for it.
drills.explanation: 3.Bb5 keeps the pressure while preparing to meet 3...f5 with 4.Nc3. After 4...fxe4 5.Nxe4 d5 White doesn't panic: 6.Nxe5 centralizes the knight and eyes f7 and c6. Black's f-file looks scary but the e5 knight, the bishop on b5, and the coming d4 break give White the steadier game — gambits must be refuted, not feared.
drills.name: Refuting the Gambit

drills.briefExplanation: 4.exf5 Nf6 5.Nc3 d5 6.d4 — take the pawn, develop, and strike back in the center.
drills.description: White to play. Black has played 3...f5 — accept the pawn and counter in the center.
drills.explanation: 4.exf5 is White's most testing reply: just take the pawn and dare Black to prove compensation. After 4...Nf6 5.Nc3 d5 White strikes with 6.d4! — opening the position while ahead in development. 6...exd4 7.Qxd4 Bxf5 looks active for Black, but White's lead in development and Black's airy kingside favor the better-prepared side.
drills.name: The exf5 Alternative

name: Schliemann Gambit — White Tactics
